draft.title: Research on AI-Enabled Learning Technologies
draft.expected_outcomes_intro: The National Science Foundation seeks to fund research that bridges computing and the learning sciences to create robust, AI-enabled educational technologies. Successful projects will yield foundational advances in how artificial intelligence systems model learner knowledge, communicate uncertainty, and provide reliable feedback, resulting in measurable improvements in learning outcomes within authentic educational environments.

expected_outcomes.text: New computational models that accurately quantify and communicate the uncertainty of AI-generated feedback to learners and educators.
Empirical evidence demonstrating how transparent, AI-driven explanations of learning progress affect student engagement and knowledge retention.

Empirical evaluation of the feasibility of integrating AI-enabled learning technologies against a specified baseline, using applicant-defined measures such as instructional time or adherence to planned teaching activities, with justified acceptance criteria.

draft.scope_intro:
Recent advances in artificial intelligence offer opportunities to personalize learning and provide adaptive feedback. However, deploying these systems in real-world educational settings exposes gaps in both computing research and the learning sciences. AI models often struggle to reliably assess complex student reasoning, fail to explain their feedback mechanisms, and lack robust measures of uncertainty when evaluating learner inputs. The pedagogical impact of these computational limitations requires investigation in authentic learning environments.

Proposals must address these dual challenges by advancing the underlying computing research—specifically focusing on the reliability, explainability, and uncertainty quantification of AI systems—while investigating the cognitive and social dimensions of how learners interact with these technologies. Research designs must include iterative testing and evaluation with learners in authentic settings, such as K-12 classrooms, university courses, or established informal learning environments.

scope.text: Develop and evaluate algorithms that improve the reliability and explainability of AI-generated feedback in educational contexts.
Conduct empirical studies with learners in authentic settings to assess the impact of AI-enabled technologies on specific learning outcomes.
Design computational methods to detect, quantify, and mitigate uncertainty in AI assessments of student knowledge or skill acquisition.
Investigate the cognitive and social dimensions of how learners interact with AI-enabled educational technologies.

exclusions.text: Proposals that solely evaluate existing, off-the-shelf commercial AI products without advancing foundational computing research are excluded.
Projects that conduct evaluations exclusively in controlled laboratory settings without deployment in authentic educational environments will not be supported.

mandatory_elements.text: The Project Description must explicitly identify the authentic learning setting where the proposed technology will be evaluated.
Proposals must detail the specific computational methods used to address AI reliability or uncertainty within the research design.
The research design must include iterative testing and evaluation with learners in authentic educational settings.

review_issues.where: call.md, Results from Prior NSF Support; call.yaml, ME3 and ME6
review_issues.problem: The prior-support trigger uses an award ending within the preceding five years. PAPPG 24-1 uses a start date within the preceding five years, together with any current funding and no-cost extensions. The call therefore incorrectly requires reporting some completed awards that started outside the window.
review_issues.fix: Replace the end-date trigger throughout both files with the PAPPG start-date trigger, retaining current funding and no-cost extensions. State the resulting window explicitly for the fictional submission date.

review_issues.where: call.md, lead eligibility paragraph; call.yaml, eligibility.consortium.notes
review_issues.problem: The Markdown restricts leads to US higher education institutions or US nonprofit research organisations. The YAML permits organisations eligible under the PAPPG and presents those two categories only as examples. Those are different eligibility rules.
review_issues.fix: Choose one eligibility rule and reproduce it identically in both files, including whether the listed organisation types are exhaustive.

review_issues.where: call.md, opening notice and Purpose and award conditions
review_issues.problem: The call explicitly invents the duration and a lead-organisation restriction. The checklist permits invention only of the topic, identifiers, budgets and dates; eligibility and duration are award conditions that must follow the real scheme. Citing the general PAPPG does not establish these solicitation-specific conditions.
review_issues.fix: Remove the invented eligibility restriction and use the applicable PAPPG eligibility rules. Ground any duration restriction in a cited real scheme, or remove the unsupported maximum. Update both files consistently.

review_issues.where: call.md, Exclusions and Required narrative; call.yaml, EX1 and EX2
review_issues.problem: The appendix and hyperlink prohibition applies only when they extend the Description beyond its limit. Standard PAPPG rules prohibit Project Description URLs and appendices unless specifically authorised; staying within the limit does not by itself make them permissible.
review_issues.fix: State the standard prohibition on Project Description URLs and appendices, including only exceptions expressly authorised by the applicable solicitation. Mirror the corrected rule in YAML.

review_issues.where: call.md, Scope introductory paragraphs; call.yaml, scope and mandatory_elements
review_issues.problem: The Markdown requires iterative testing with learners and investigation of both cognitive and social dimensions of learner interaction. Neither requirement is captured in the YAML. Authentic-setting empirical studies alone do not establish iteration or coverage of those dimensions.
review_issues.fix: Add distinct YAML requirements for iterative learner testing and the required cognitive and social investigations, with matching Markdown wording, or remove those obligations from the Markdown.

review_issues.where: call.md, Exclusions and Specific conditions and mandatory elements; call.yaml, EX1–EX2 and ME1–ME6
review_issues.problem: The appendix/hyperlink exclusion appears twice, and all three initial mandatory elements are repeated verbatim. Separate identifiers make identical requirements appear to be independent assessment items and can double-count compliance.
review_issues.fix: Delete EX2 and the duplicate ME4–ME6 entries, remove the corresponding repeated Markdown bullets, and update identifiers or references consistently.

review_issues.where: call.md, third Expected outcomes bullet; call.yaml, EO3
review_issues.problem: A 'validated framework' that operates 'without disrupting existing pedagogical workflows' has no defined validation target or operational meaning for disruption. The absolute wording also leaves unclear whether ordinary changes needed to introduce a learning technology constitute failure.
review_issues.fix: Require empirical evaluation of integration feasibility against a specified baseline, using applicant-defined measures such as teacher workload, instructional time or adherence to planned teaching activities, with justified acceptance criteria.
